claims.text: Peds (Siklos): indicated ≥ 2 y w sickle cell anemia and recurrent moderate–severe painful crises, to ↓ crises and transfusions;
claims.quote: is indicated to reduce the frequency of painful crises and to reduce the need for blood transfusions in adult and pediatric patients, 2 years of age and older, with sickle cell anemia with recurrent moderate to severe painful crises

claims.text: start 20 mg/kg once daily (actual or ideal wt, whichever is less);
claims.quote: Pediatrics: 20 mg/kg once daily based on patient's actual or ideal weight, whichever is less.
Monitor the patient's blood count every 2 weeks

claims.text: → macrocytosis, which can mask folate deficiency: give prophylactic folic acid.
claims.quote: DROXIA causes macrocytosis, which may mask the incidental development of folic acid deficiency. Prophylactic administration of folic acid is recommended.

claims.text: Contraception during tx and after: females ± 6 months, males ± 1 yr.
claims.quote: Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during and after treatment with DROXIA for at least 6 months after therapy. Advise males of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during and after treatment with DROXIA for at least 1 year after therapy

Avoid use of live vaccine in patients taking DROXIA. Concomitant use of DROXIA with a live virus vaccine may potentiate the replication of the virus and/or may increase the adverse reaction of the vaccine because normal defense mechanisms may be suppressed by DROXIA. Vaccination with live vaccines in a patient receiving DROXIA may result in severe infection.

claims.text: W antiretrovirals (didanosine, stavudine): pancreatitis, hepatotoxicity, periph neuropathy.
claims.quote: Pancreatitis, hepatotoxicity, and peripheral neuropathy have occurred when hydroxyurea was administered concomitantly with antiretroviral drugs, including didanosine and stavudine
claims.locator: 5.7 Risks with Concomitant Use of Antiretroviral Drugs
